title: S3 for Rails attachments: private objects and signed access
outcome: Set up private object storage and trace metadata, upload, authorization, and download separately.
benefits: Shared durable object storage without app-local upload disks.
drawbacks: Metadata consistency, URL lifetime, lifecycle, and transfer costs need design.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: DB owns permission and meaning. S3 owns bytes.

trace.title: Authorized metadata
trace.detail: S3 stores objects addressed by bucket and key. A slash in a key is a naming convention, not a filesystem directory with ordinary POSIX behavior. Keep application metadata and access rules in the database; the object is the bytes.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
User requests attachment → Rails authorizes record → app issues allowed key/URL → browser uploads bytes → app verifies completion and saves metadata → later read rechecks access before issuing a download.

Test the crash between upload and metadata save. Orphan cleanup must distinguish abandoned objects from live references. For immediate revocation needs, consider the lifetime of already issued URLs.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A public bucket can bypass Rails permission checks. Reusing a key can replace an existing object according to the operation/versioning contract. A presigned URL should not be logged as harmless metadata.
